newsitem.title: USA: Fed nominee Gramlich sees healthy economy -- CNBC.
newsitem.headline: Fed nominee Gramlich sees healthy economy -- CNBC.

text.p: Edward Gramlich, President Bill Clinton's choice for one of two openings at the Federal Reserve Board, characterized the U.S. economy as "pretty good" with low inflation.
Gramlich was speaking to U.S. cable television network CNBC in an interview from the University of Michigan at Ann Arbor, where he is currently a professor of economics.

"If you want me to characterize the state of the economy ... it's pretty good; inflation is quiescent. The unemployment rate is close to historic lows, and that's a very good combination," Gramlich said.
He declined further comment on the economy, and refused to say how he would have voted at the Fed's last policy-setting meeting had he attended it. That meeting was held on July 1 and 2.
Gramlich, regarded as an economist known for his pragmatism and consensus building, was formally nominated by Clinton on Thursday, and now faces Senate approval.
